title: Decide and apply pylint config tuning for convention-mismatch checks
description:
Once daz-mcp-server-wdk and daz-mcp-server-cpx land, re-run pylint with a properly-installed environment and the corrected version matrix to get an accurate baseline (locally verified at 4.41/10 as of this writing, see epic daz-mcp-server-lkb for the full category breakdown). Before working through the ~1500 remaining findings category-by-category, decide which checks are genuinely valuable for this codebase's conventions vs. which are structural false positives that should be disabled/tuned rather than 'fixed':

Strong candidates for disabling or reconfiguring (likely false-positive-by-design, not real defects):
- redefined-outer-name (190 hits): almost certainly pytest fixtures used as test-function parameters -- the correct, idiomatic pytest pattern, not a bug. Standard practice is to disable this check for the tests/ directory (or globally, since pytest fixtures are pervasive here).
- unused-argument (354 hits): likely dominated by two false-positive-prone patterns -- (a) @mcp.tool() function parameters whose signature is dictated by the tool schema Claude calls, not by internal logic, and (b) pytest fixture parameters requested only for their side effects/skip behavior (see conftest.py's live_client, figure_label, etc.). Needs a sample audit to confirm the ratio of real vs. false positives before deciding whether to disable outright or tune per-directory.
- missing-function-docstring / missing-class-docstring / missing-module-docstring (387+99+5 = 491 hits): a real decision point, not a clear false positive -- see the docstring category issue for the systematic-fix track if the team wants these actually written rather than disabled.

Needs real investigation (not obviously a false positive, don't disable without looking):
- no-name-in-module (158) / no-member (67): could be genuine dynamic-attribute patterns in dazpy/fastmcp that pylint's static analysis can't see (may need targeted # pylint: disable comments or stub files rather than a blanket config change), or could be flagging real bugs. Sample and categorize before deciding.
- broad-exception-caught (58): this codebase's tool functions deliberately catch broad Exception to route into handle_dazpy_error's typed-exception dispatch (see vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py) -- likely intentional and correct given the design, but worth a quick confirm rather than assuming.

Output of this issue: an agreed .pylintrc (or [tool.pylint] section in pyproject.toml) checked in, plus a documented rationale (in the file itself, as comments, or in this issue's notes) for what's disabled and why -- so the next person touching pylint config understands the reasoning instead of rediscovering it.
close_reason: Already done — pyproject.toml's [tool.pylint.messages_control] and [tool.pylint.similarities] sections (plus pylint.yml's tests/-scoped disables) deliver exactly what this issue asked for: broad-exception-caught investigated and disabled with rationale; redefined-outer-name/unused-argument deliberately scoped to tests/ only (not blanket-disabled) with src/ remainder tracked in r13; no-name-in-module/no-member investigated, found to be real stale imports (not false positives), left enabled, tracked in ful; missing-*-docstring decision made (real gap, tracked in dk7, not suppressed); duplicate-code tuned to min-similarity-lines=8 with rationale, residual tracked in cw8. All comments cite this issue by name. Verified 2026-09-08.

title: pylint.yml: install project dependencies before running pylint
description:
Root cause of the ~90+ import-error (E0401/no-name-in-module) findings that dominate the current 'Your code has been rated at 3.46/10' CI score: .github/workflows/pylint.yml's 'Install dependencies' step only runs 'pip install pylint', never installing the project itself or its runtime dependencies (httpx, fastmcp, dazpy). Pylint therefore cannot resolve a single third-party import anywhere in the ~137-tool codebase.

Fix: add a step (or extend the existing one) to install the project and its dependencies before the pylint step, e.g. 'pip install -e .' plus the dev tools currently declared under [dependency-groups] dev in pyproject.toml (pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx) since pylint also needs those importable for the tests/ directory.

Verified locally: reinstalling properly (uv venv; uv pip install -e .; uv pip install pytest pytest-asyncio respx pylint) and re-running 'pylint $(git ls-files *.py)' raises the score from 3.46/10 to 4.41/10 and removes the import-error noise, leaving the real, addressable findings visible (see epic daz-mcp-server-lkb for the full category breakdown).

Note: dazpy itself will resolve to whatever version is on PyPI (2.6.0 as of this writing) unless a specific version/local install is pinned -- that's fine for pylint's purposes (it only needs the import to resolve, not runtime behavior).
close_reason: Stale — already fixed in commit 0e6151d ('fix(ci): install project and dev dependencies before running pylint'). Verified 2026-09-08: .github/workflows/pylint.yml's Install dependencies step runs 'pip install -e .' plus pylint/pytest/pytest-asyncio/respx, matching this issue's proposed fix exactly.

title: DazBusyError/StudioBusyError/ConcurrencyLimitError don't exist in any published dazpy release yet
description: Discovered while investigating pylint no-member findings for daz-mcp-server-ful. src/vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py:39 does 'isinstance(exc, daz_exc.DazBusyError)' as part of the studio-busy-handling feature (merged via PR #4 / commit 906cd88 'feat: surface DazBusyError as a clear ToolError to MCP tool callers'), and tests/test_errors.py references daz_exc.StudioBusyError and daz_exc.ConcurrencyLimitError. None of these three names exist in dazpy.exceptions in any version currently on PyPI (checked up through 2.7.2, the latest published as of this writing; pyproject.toml pins dazpy>=2.6.0). Per report, DazBusyError ships in daz-script-server 2.8.0, which has not been published to PyPI yet -- this whole feature was built/tested against a pre-release dazpy. Effect: _errors.py:39 will raise AttributeError the moment handle_dazpy_error() runs against ANY exception in a real deployment (attribute lookup happens at call time), and tests/test_errors.py's three busy-error tests fail at collection/run time with AttributeError since dazpy.exceptions.StudioBusyError doesn't exist. Fix: once dazpy 2.8.0 (or whichever version actually ships DazBusyError) is published, bump pyproject.toml's dazpy>=2.6.0 pin to require it, and reconcile test_errors.py's StudioBusyError/ConcurrencyLimitError names with _errors.py's actual DazBusyError (single class vs two, matching whatever the real dazpy 2.8.0 API turns out to be).
acceptance_criteria: pyproject.toml requires a dazpy version that actually publishes DazBusyError; _errors.py and test_errors.py use matching, real exception class names; pylint --enable=no-member src/vangard_daz_mcp/_errors.py tests/test_errors.py reports zero findings.
notes: Blocked on an external dependency (dazpy/daz-script-server 2.8.0 publication to PyPI) -- not fixable purely within this repo until that ships.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/pylint-ci branch (commit d4dbe50). dazpy 2.8.0 -- which publishes DazBusyError, StudioBusyError, and ConcurrencyLimitError -- was tagged and released to PyPI (bluemoonfoundry/daz-script-server v2.8.0 tag pushed, release workflow completed successfully). Bumped pyproject.toml's dazpy>=2.6.0 pin to dazpy>=2.8.0. Verified against the real published 2.8.0 wheel: pylint --enable=no-member on _errors.py and test_errors.py is clean (10.00/10), and all 7 tests in test_errors.py pass. title: pylint.yml: trim Python version matrix to match requires-python
description:
pylint.yml's build matrix runs python-version ["3.8", "3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"], but pyproject.toml declares requires-python = ">=3.11". The project doesn't claim to support 3.8-3.10 anywhere else (uses PEP 604 unions like 'list[str] | None' throughout, which is fine for pylint's astroid parser but signals the project's actual target), so three of the five CI matrix legs are testing versions the project isn't meant to run on at all -- wasted CI time and a source of version-specific noise unrelated to real code quality.

Fix: trim the matrix to ["3.11", "3.12"] to match the declared support window (add 3.13 too if the team wants to track it, otherwise keep to the two currently-declared-supported minors).

Discovered alongside daz-mcp-server-wdk while investigating why the pylint CI check has never passed since it was added (2026-05-08).

description:
The Pylint CI check (.github/workflows/pylint.yml) has failed on every push to master since it was added on 2026-05-08 -- confirmed via 'gh run list --branch master' showing failures on every recorded run. It currently reports 'Your code has been rated at 3.46/10', but that number is itself misleading: the workflow only runs 'pip install pylint' before analysis, never installing the project's own dependencies (httpx, fastmcp, dazpy, pytest, etc.), so pylint can't resolve any third-party import anywhere in the codebase. Reinstalling properly (uv venv + pip install -e . + dev deps) and re-running locally gives a truer baseline of 4.41/10 with this category breakdown across the whole repo (git ls-files '*.py'):

  387 missing-function-docstring     58 broad-exception-caught
  354 unused-argument                41 unused-import
  190 redefined-outer-name           21 protected-access
  158 no-name-in-module              16 duplicate-code
   99 missing-class-docstring        15 import-outside-toplevel
   79 line-too-long                  10 too-many-arguments
   67 no-member                      10 too-many-positional-arguments
                                      10 superfluous-parens
                                       8 invalid-name
                                       6 global-statement
                                       5 missing-module-docstring
                                       4 unsubscriptable-object

This is a codebase that has never been pylint-clean since the check was introduced -- the workflow was added without ever bringing the code up to its default ruleset or tuning that ruleset to the project's actual conventions (e.g. pytest fixture patterns necessarily trigger 'redefined-outer-name' and 'unused-argument' by design, which is not a real defect). Discovered while working on the DazBusyError busy-handling PR (#4) when its CI checks came back failing for reasons entirely unrelated to that PR's 2-file diff.

Goal: a CI gate that (a) actually reflects real code quality rather than environment misconfiguration, and (b) the team can trust as a real signal going forward, achieved by fixing the two mechanical CI bugs, deciding + applying sane config tuning for convention-mismatch checks, and then working through the remaining real findings by category.

This epic is closed once all its child issues (CI fixes, config tuning decision, and each finding-category task) are closed.
close_reason: All 13 children complete. Pylint CI now passes for real (not just the --fail-under=7.0 gate on a broken environment): src 9.75/10, tests 9.97/10, verified 2026-09-08 with a fresh in-venv pylint 4.0.8 matching the exact CI invocation in .github/workflows/pylint.yml. The two CI mechanical bugs (deps not installed, version matrix mismatch) were fixed; convention-mismatch checks were tuned with documented rationale (broad-exception-caught, too-many-arguments/positional-arguments disabled repo-wide; redefined-outer-name/unused-argument/missing-docstrings/import-outside-toplevel scoped to tests/ only); and every real finding category (docstrings, unused imports, protected-access, duplicate-code, line-too-long, unused-argument audit, no-name-in-module/no-member, superfluous-parens, invalid-name, global-statement) was either fixed or resolved to zero. 192 tests pass throughout.

title: Test suite imports broken across 17 files after server.py refactor split
description: Commit 2e9fbbf (feat(refactor): split 15K-line server.py into 13 focused tool modules, 2026-06-26) split the monolithic server.py into tools/*.py + _mcp.py + _client.py + _registry.py, but the test suite was never updated. 17 of 18 files under tests/ still do 'from vangard_daz_mcp.server import (...)' expecting ~130 names (nearly every tool function, plus _register_scripts, CONTENT_BROWSER_URL, and module state _http_client/_content_browser_client) that no longer live in server.py -- it is now a 15-line entrypoint. This breaks pytest collection for the entire tests/ directory (conftest.py fails to import, which cascades to every test file via fixture discovery). Discovered while implementing the DazBusyError MCP-side wiring (feature/studio-busy-handling branch) -- worked around there with pytest --noconftest on an isolated new test file, but the pre-existing suite itself needs a real fix. Two options considered but not decided: (1) restore ~130 re-exports in server.py (one file, minimal diff, restores tests' existing assumption), or (2) rewrite each of the 17 test files' imports to point at the correct submodule (vangard_daz_mcp.tools.camera_light, .scene, ._registry, ._client, etc. -- more files touched but keeps the refactor's module boundaries clean). May already be partially addressed by in-progress uncommitted work on phase4_tools_implementation (dirty changes to morph.py and test_actors_integration.py at time of discovery) -- check that branch's state before starting.
close_reason: Stale — no longer reproduces. Verified 2026-09-08: zero test files import from vangard_daz_mcp.server (grep clean across tests/), pytest --collect-only collects all 529/531 tests with no errors, and the full suite passes (192 passed -m 'not integration and not slow'). Must have been fixed by intervening work since this was filed 2026-07-22; no corresponding fix commit identified, but current state is unambiguously healthy.

title: Add daz_wait_for_scene_event using GET /scene/events SSE stream
description: The daz-script-server now exposes GET /scene/events as a Server-Sent Events stream with categories: node, skeleton, light, camera, selection, scene, time, render. Filter with ?filter=render,scene etc. Events include render.started, render.finished, scene.loaded, scene.saved, node.added, selection.primary_changed, time.changed (debounced 150ms), playback.started, etc. Add a daz_wait_for_scene_event(event_types: list[str], timeout_seconds: int = 30) MCP tool that opens an SSE connection, parses event frames (data: {type, ts, data}\n\n), and returns when one of the requested types fires or timeout is reached. Most immediately useful: waiting for render.finished after daz_render(), detecting scene.loaded after daz_load_file(). Uses httpx streaming (client.stream). Add mock tests using respx streaming mock.
close_reason: Implemented daz_wait_for_scene_event with SSE streaming via GET /scene/events; 7 mock tests added to test_server.py, all passing.

title: Add daz_save_scene_copy using POST /scene/save-copy endpoint

The daz-script-server now has POST /scene/save-copy which handles this correctly: for clean scenes it does a pure file copy (no DAZ API calls); for dirty scenes it saves to the dest path then restores the original filename. Add a new daz_save_scene_copy(path) MCP tool that calls this endpoint and returns {ok, path, source, method}. Add mock tests in test_server.py verifying it calls /scene/save-copy and not the script registry.

title: Harvest Strand-Based Hair creation/listing, add tests + honor UI-action caveat (fork 0d85827)
description:
Cherry-pick blackbyte-fork/master commit 0d85827 (https://github.com/BlackByteDE/daz-mcp-server) onto our master. Adds Strand-Based Hair node creation and listing tools -- a real capability gap (no hair tools exist today), but scoped narrowly: creation + listing only, styling explicitly out of reach and documented as such by the fork author.

Evaluation verdict: Utility Medium-High but narrow. description:
